_readme: Which binder PDFs the repository keeps. Content is data; the mechanic is pbr_binder_retention.py.
THE RULE: a binder is deleted permanently once it has been parsed with no issues, and kept otherwise.
A PDF attachment is evidence that is sighted, parsed and screened. It is not a repository artefact and
*.pdf is ignored by git, so 'delete' here means delete from disk: there is no copy behind it.
WHAT 'PARSED WITH NO ISSUES' HAS TO MEAN. Deleting the binder forecloses every check that can only be
run against the page, so each condition below is one such check, already run and already recorded:
corpus              the batch was parsed at all. A binder with no corpus is unparsed evidence.
page_text           every document retains its page text, so the shingle check keeps an independent
haystack. Without it the verbatim check returns UNVERIFIABLE, and UNVERIFIABLE is
not a pass, so the wording could never be checked against the page again.
gate_not_red        the corpus passes its own gate. A RED corpus is never built from and will need
re-extraction, which needs the binder back.
mask_record         an M1 record exists naming THIS binder by md5. The fill is not in the text layer,
so the masked-row verdict is the one finding no retained text can reproduce. The
md5 must match the file on disk or the record describes a different document.
no_hold_record      the batch is not held. A hold record is outstanding work against the page.
A binder failing any condition is KEPT and the reason is printed. Nothing is deleted on a dry run.

protect.why: Not attachments. The two standing Council reference documents the JSON captures in data/reference/ were made from, and the authority those captures are verified against.
